sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Thermal Insulation and Refractory Ceramic Brick Masonry for Kilns

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France has an extensive network of approximately 100 active bilateral investment treaties. The precise applicable treaty is determined after UBO nationality screening. Representative treaties include the France-Germany Investment Protection Treaty (1960), France-Italy Investment Treaty (1958), France-China BIT (2007), and France-Hong Kong BIT (1997).
France is a party to the Energy Charter Treaty (1994, in force 1998) and the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (New York, 1958).

Relevant tax treaty framework includes the France-United States DTA (1994, as amended by protocols signed in 2006 and 2009) and the France-China DTA (2013), as applicable based on the ultimate beneficial owner's residence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT framework is set out in the Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-49 and R.561-1 et seq. (customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification, PEP screening, record keeping, and suspicious transaction reporting). The beneficial ownership register for companies is established by Code de commerce (CoC), Articles L.123-3-1, L.123-3-2 and R.123-208-1 to R.123-208-9, as introduced by Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Loi Sapin II) and Décret n° 2017-1094 du 22 juin 2017 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign incorporation certificate or equivalent corporate register extract for any corporate shareholder or manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or other official authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the source country is not a Hague member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted to the French incorporation agent or attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or other competent issuing authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity copies of all proposed managers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization if certified abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or governmental certificate) for each individual UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or local governmental authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, consular legalization, or recognized notarized certification depending on country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of banking reference letter confirming the business relationship and source of funds (for AML/KYC purposes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in the UBO's or shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if required by French banks or the registered agent; otherwise bank certification plus sworn translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, proposed managers, and authorized signatories against (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists and Council Regulations; (iii) French domestic asset-freezing measures issued by the Direction Générale du Trésor under CMF Articles L.151-1 et seq.; and (iv) OFAC's SDN list as a risk-management enhancement. PEP screening is mandatory under CMF Article L.561-10, including French national PEPs and foreign politically exposed persons, with enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk third countries identified by FATF and EU Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675. Filings and KYC documents must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; RCS pre-verification may be performed via infogreffe.fr.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names, constitutional documents, and registration filings must be in French. The name must be written using the Latin alphabet with appropriate French accents; if a name is derived from a non-Latin script, a certified French transliteration is mandatory. The name must not be contrary to public order (ordre public) or misleading, and it must be available under Article L.123-1-1 of the Code de commerce and relevant case law on distinctive character.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a standalone statutory name-reservation system; name clearance is assessed at the moment of RCS registration. Where the Greffe or INPI formally rejects a name, the applicant may submit a written re-examination request with legal arguments demonstrating distinctiveness and absence of conflict. If the refusal persists, the applicant may petition the Juge Commis à la Surveillance du Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (commercial court supervision judge) within ten days of the refusal, and further appeal to the Cour d'appel. Name search certificates or private availability opinions are refreshed every 30 days prior to filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office formation is permissible for an SARL using an approved business domiciliation company under Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-1 et seq. and R.123-141-1 et seq., provided the domiciliary has a physical address in France, is registered with the Préfecture, and offers secretariat and reception services. This is acceptable for the refractory masonry contracting industry because the activity does not require a statutory operating license; however, the company must maintain an operational site or project address for performance of services.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/AML identity verification, PEP and sanctions screening, and corporate background checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed legal and compliance service provider engaged by the incorporators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk commercial contracting entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by French regulations on greffe fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per insertion line (approximately €4 per line, variable by department)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents for all UBOs and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, consulates, or notary in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular and certification fees, plus courier expenses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translations of articles, powers of attorney, and supporting documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per French translator tariff schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement with an approved French business domiciliation company (12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, typically €400–€600 per year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company corporate kit, statutory registers, seals, and bank-required dossier preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal stationer and notary services provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French legal counsel for drafting the articles of association, handling the pre-incorporation clearance, and completing the RCS registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SARL incorporation; fixed fee plus disbursements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (France), Livre II, Titre II, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), together with R.123-1 et seq.; Law n°2008-776 (LME) abolishing minimum capital; Law n°2019-486 (PACTE) and Decree n°2021-300 providing for the single electronic filing portal (Guichet unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce for the registered-office district, operating through the Guichet unique managed by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; post-registration records are maintained in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive statuts executed by all shareholders, together with the single legal-form registration dossier (télédossier de création d'entreprise, successor to the former M0/S0 forms), submitted via the Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for a French SARL; the capital is fixed freely in the statuts and must be fully subscribed. Cash contributions must be paid at least to one-fifth (20%) at constitution, unless the statuts require full release; any balance must be paid within five years. The cash is deposited in a blocked escrow account opened for the company in formation, and the bank's attestation de blocage is released only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST SHAREHOLDER RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] SARL. The undersigned incorporators, acting as the general meeting, unanimously resolve: (1) to approve the constitutive statuts dated [DATE]; (2) to ratify the full subscription of [NUMBER] equal-value cash shares; (3) to accept the blocked capital deposit certificate and approve its release upon RCS registration; (4) to adopt the registered office at [SITE ADDRESS]; (5) to appoint [FULL NAME] as gérant for an indefinite term, with authority to open bank accounts, sign contracts, and perform all corporate formalities; and (6) to grant the gérant signatory mandates before banks, tax authorities, insurers, and the RCS. Adopted unanimously and recorded in the corporate minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation corporate name clearance, registered-office domiciliation and statut drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI/Data-RCS name-availability databases and the Greffe du tribunal de commerce for the planned registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a corporate-name and trademark availability search in the French RCS and INPI databases; verify that the proposed corporate name, object and activity wording are lawful; select the registered office (lease, co-working, or gérant's home under applicable domiciliation rules); prepare the draft statuts with the share capital structure, cash subscriptions, nominee of gérant and corporate objects covering refractory masonry and thermal insulation.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each shareholder
Proof of residential address of each shareholder
Domiciliation contract, notarized lease or property title for the registered office
Proposed corporate name and availability search result
Source-of-funds and enhanced KYC statement for each cash contributor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is likely to conflict with a protected RCS company name or trademark, choose a new distinctive name and repeat the search; no registry approval is needed at this stage, and corrections are made by amending the draft statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the blocked escrow account and depositing the paid-up portion of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a French notary for notarized cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the SARL en formation; deposit at least 20% of the cash subscriptions (or 100% if the statuts so require); ensure the bank identifies the subscribers and the exact capital breakdown; obtain the attestation de blocage de fonds addressed to the RCS registrar. Foreign shareholders must provide a SWIFT reference and certified identity so the bank may complete anti-money-laundering checks.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts
Identity documents and proof of address of each shareholder
KYC and beneficial-ownership declarations
Source-of-funds documentation
Bank deposit instruction signed by all subscribers or their appointed representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries or refuses the deposit, cure the KYC deficiency, provide a translated source-of-funds statement, or redirect the deposit to the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the attestation is reissued after compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of constitutive statuts and the first shareholder resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The shareholders acting directly in an acte sous seing privé, or a French notaire where a deed or real-estate contribution is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize and date the statuts; have each shareholder sign the signature page, physically or through a recognized qualified electronic signature process; include the gérant's dated consent to appointment; execute the pro-forma first shareholder resolution; where contributions consist of real estate, industrial property or shares requiring formal transfer, obtain authenticated notarial deeds and independent valuation before filing.
required_dossiers: Final signed statuts
Act of subscription and payment of shares (acte de souscription)
Gérant's written acceptance and consent
Declaration of non-conviction of the gérant
Notarial deed, if applicable
First shareholder resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If signatures or annexes are defective, replace the affected pages with corrected versions and have all shareholders initial the rectification; if notarial authentication is refused, correct the legal condition and re-execute the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Single-window electronic filing with the Guichet unique and RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique portal; competent Greffe du tribunal de commerce; Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete creation dossier in the 'Création d'entreprise' flow at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; select 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'; upload the signed statuts and all required annexes; pay the registry filing duty; the system transmits the dossier to the Greffe, INSEE, DGFiP, URSSAF and relevant social bodies. The Greffe verifies legal completeness, enters the company in the RCS, and delivers the Kbis extract and the SIREN number.
required_dossiers: Electronically or manually signed statuts
Bank attestation de blocage de fonds
Gérant's declaration of non-conviction
Identity document and proof of address of the gérant
Registered-office domiciliation certificate
Accepted certificate for the publication of incorporation notice, if requested by the Guichet unique workflow
Completed and signed Guichet unique summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI coordinator or Greffe raises a query, access the platform notice, upload the missing or corrected document within the stated period and request expedited review; if the dossier is rejected, correct all defects and file a fresh complete dossier through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration activation: insurance, tax/social registrations and release of blocked capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS/Greffe; DGFiP; URSSAF; authorized insurance carrier or broker; commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Kbis, procure professional civil liability and mandatory décennale construction insurance covering refractory and thermal-insulation works; obtain the VAT/TVA number from the DGFiP; finalize employer and payroll registration with URSSAF; present the Kbis, the insurance certificate and the certified company resolution to the depository bank to convert the blocked account into the operating account and release capital.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Insurance certificate or cover note for civil liability and décennale insurance
VAT number confirmation from DGFiP
URSSAF employer registration receipt
Gérant's bank signature resolution and company-by-laws excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If insurance is not issued immediately, obtain a temporary cover note from the carrier or through the mandatory construction-insurance declaration mechanism; if the bank delays release, provide the complete Kbis, insurance certificate and corporate bank mandate resolution to satisfy the bank's post-registration due diligence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable at company level; no separate industrial operating licence is required for a mobile refractory-masonry and thermal-insulation contracting SARL in France. Worksite and environmental compliance is supervised by the DREETS/DREAL and by the relevant local unit when the company intervenes on an ICPE-classified client facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; the RCS registration is the sole commercial authorization. The company may voluntarily obtain Qualibat professional certification for refractory and thermal-insulation works, and must carry mandatory professional civil liability plus décennale construction insurance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), as territorial delegate of the Ministry for Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category C — the contractor operates no fixed installation requiring an environmental impact assessment; EIA obligations, when any, arise at the client's industrial facility project under the ICPE regime (Code de l'environnement, Articles L.181-1 et seq.).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the contractor's own activities. During works on client facilities, the contractor must respect the client's ICPE authorization or registration conditions, including dust and VOC workplace thresholds, management of refractory-ceramic-fiber waste under the European Waste Catalogue and CLP/REACH obligations, and discharge prohibitions applicable to washout water from refractory demolition works.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Company offices, workshop and storage areas must satisfy standard fire-safety, structural load and workplace health rules and are monitored by the labor inspectorate. On client industrial boiler sites, the company must obtain and follow the site fire permit (permis feu), apply ATEX-zone restrictions, use a method statement for hot refractory work, implement working-at-height protection, provide PPE, and complete mandatory occupational health checks and asbestos-awareness training before handling old insulation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; primary portals: impots.gouv.fr (fiscal identity, VAT returns, company file) and formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique operated with INPI for SIREN/SIRET allocation and automatic VAT registration). Customs export competences are exercised by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) through the DELTA/LEX electronic clearance platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned French SARL: (1) File all constitutive formalities through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) attaching the articles of association, the gérant's identity document, proof of registered office and the anti-money-laundering declarations; INPI/INSEE delivers the SIREN (9 digits), SIRET (14 digits), the NAF/APE activity code and the Kbis extract. (2) The Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) automatically allocates the intra-Community VAT identification number (format FR + 2 check digits + SIREN) after registration is completed; this is evidenced by the Kbis extract and the avis de situation SIRENE. (3) A foreign entity with no French permanent establishment must instead file Form Cerfa No. 13826*04 (demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA intracommunautaire pour un assujetti non établi) with the DGFiP non-resident tax unit, and, if not established in the EU, must appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) jointly and severally liable for VAT under Article 289 A CGI. (4) The SARL must additionally obtain an EORI number (FR + SIREN) from the DGDDI through the electronic EORI/DELTA service before lodging any export declaration. All post-registration changes (manager, registered office, activity, cessation) must be declared through the Guichet Unique within 30 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Available mechanisms: (1) Article 239 bis AA CGI: a SARL whose shareholders are exclusively physical persons may opt irrevocably within five years of creation for corporate-tax transparency (pass-through taxation of partners at impôt sur le revenu), with the option being filed via the annual income tax return; otherwise the SARL is definitively opaque and subject to corporation tax (IS). (2) Article 206-3 CGI: a default pass-through partnership (SNC, SCI) may elect compulsory entity-level IS. (3) Article 256 C CGI and article 22 decies of the annex: election to form a TVA group (Groupe TVA) among closely connected established French entities, with the représentant membre filing a single VAT return. (4) Hybrid mismatch treatment: ATAD 2 is implemented by Articles 212 bis and 212 sexies CGI; there is no domestic unilateral election, so the foreign classification of a hybrid entity determines the application of the neutralisation rules. (5) Customs elections relevant to the refractory activity include outward processing (perfectionnement passif) and drawback regimes enabling duty/VAT suspension or remission for exported processed goods.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) - French Value Added Tax implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for non-established foreign suppliers: any taxable supply deemed to take place in France triggers registration (or OSS declaration) from the first euro of turnover, and the franchise en base de TVA of Article 293 B CGI is unavailable to non-established entities. Intra-EU distance sales of goods to private consumers and B2C electronically supplied services may be remitted through the OSS system without separate French VAT registration up to a pan-European EUR 10,000 annual turnover ceiling (Article 296-0 ter CGI). French-established small operators enjoy the franchise en base de TVA unified at EUR 85,000 annual turnover (goods and services) effective 1 January 2025; exceeding this threshold makes VAT registration compulsory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B domestic e-invoicing (facturation électronique) applies in waves: all French-established businesses must be able to receive structured e-invoices from 1 September 2026; large enterprises and ETIs must issue via a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the public PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) of DGFiP from 1 September 2026; SMEs and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027. Permitted formats are FACTUR-X (hybrid), UBL 2.1 and CII, and invoices must contain the mandatory mentions of Article 242 nonies A CGI. Cross-border supplies do not require e-invoicing but must be reported through the e-reporting channel (transaction and payment data) to DGFiP on the same timeline. The architecture uses PDP-to-PDP APIs and the DGFiP central directory, creating near-real-time transmission (within one working day of issuance), but France does not operate per-transaction fiscal stamping by the tax authority; retail cash registers remain subject to the NF 525 anti-fraud software certification (Law No. 2018-898).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: tangible movable goods (refractory bricks, ceramic modules, castable/pre-cast refractory shapes) sold and definitively dispatched or carried outside EU customs territory by or on behalf of the supplier are exempt at 0% under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided physical exit is proven. Intra-EU supplies to a VAT-identified customer are exempt under Article 262 ter CGI with a valid VIES number, transport evidence and submission of the EC sales list (DES). Services nuance for refractory lining: (a) on-site masonry and relining performed on kilns and boilers physically attached to land or buildings in France are supplies of services connected with immovable property taxable in France at 20% under Article 259 A CGI, even for a foreign principal; no 0% zero-rating is available, but the foreign customer may recover French input VAT through the non-established taxable person refund procedure (Article 271 CGI / 8th Directive portal). (b) Services performed on movable refractory equipment (removable boiler sections, ladles, torpedo cars, detached modules) for a foreign customer whose goods are exported may qualify for the exemption under Article 262-II-1° and -2° CGI if the customs declaration, transport documents and service contract evidence the direct link with the export. (c) Outward processing (perfectionnement passif) permits duty/TVA-suspended treatment for foreign-owned refractory goods processed in France and re-exported to the principal; the service invoice can then benefit from the 0% export exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration Unique d'Exportation / DAU-EAD) with the MRN (Movement Reference Number) issued via DELTA/LEX and the customs office of exit certificate proving departure from EU territory.
Bill of Lading (maritime), CMR road consignment note (Genève Convention), Air Waybill, multimodal bill, or GPS/terminal exit records as transport evidence evidencing the goods left France and the EU.

Commercial Invoice and Packing List with precise HS classification (refractory articles of headings 6902/6903), Incoterms, EUR currency, and reference to the underlying order and the SARL export contract.
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT or attestation de change proving export proceeds credited in EUR to the French bank account of the SARL.

For intra-EU supplies: buyer's VIES VAT validation output, EC Sales List (état récapitulatif clients / DES) filed on impots.gouv.fr, transport ticket showing delivery in another Member State, and the customer's purchase order.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP export audits (vérification de comptabilité) cross-match MRN/DAU data from the customs DELTA system with bank inflows, transport tickets, downstream customer reconstruction and the accounting trail. Standard VAT reassessment is 3 years (Livre des procédures fiscales Article L. 169), extended to 10 years in case of concealed activity or fraud, and to 6 years for cross-border operations. A false or fictitious export zero-rating triggers: (1) retroactive VAT clawback reinvoiced at 20% on the full taxable amount; (2) the 80% penalty of Article 1729 CGI for manœuvres frauduleuses or opposition à contrôle; (3) late-payment interest at 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI; (4) criminal VAT-fraud prosecution under Article 1741 CGI (up to 5 years imprisonment, EUR 500,000 fine, confiscation, publication and exclusion from public procurement); (5) customs penalties under Code des douanes Articles 413-1 to 414 (fines of one to two times the embezzled sums plus confiscation of goods and vehicle where applicable); and (6) joint and several liability of the fiscal representative (Article 289 A CGI), personal liability of the gérant for administrative penalties, and disqualification risks where organised fraud (fraude carrousel/fly-by-night) is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (in coordination with the European Central Bank for Eurozone monetary policy and with the French Treasury for cross-border capital reporting under the French Monetary and Financial Code)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully liberalised exchange control regime as a Eurozone member. Current account convertibility is unrestricted under EU Treaty articles on free movement of capital (Article 64 TFEU) and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). Capital account transactions are also free, subject only to statistical reporting thresholds, EU financial sanctions, and anti-money laundering obligations. Profit remittances by a SARL to non-resident shareholders are permitted without prior ministerial authorisation; a withholding tax may apply unless an EU tax treaty or the Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces or eliminates it. No lingering exchange control approval is required for EUR-denominated transfers, and foreign currency accounts may be held domestically with authorised banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender or forced conversion into EUR exists in France or the Eurozone. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency revenues in authorised foreign currency accounts. However, for balance-of-payments statistics purposes, French resident companies must report each cross-border transaction with a non-resident counterparty when the individual transaction amount exceeds €50,000, and a monthly aggregated declaration is required when the cumulative amount exceeds €750,000, filed with the Banque de France through calibrated reporting channels (reporting code 'SURRI' or the Banque de France 'Balance des Paiements' portal). Invoicing in EUR is standard but not compulsory.

Operational Account with FX Hedging and Export Credit Facilities

Operational Escrow-able Account for Domestic Receivables and Public Sector Contracts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for SME Contracting and Import/Export Settlement
Capital Escrow Account (for inbound capital injections and secured disbursement structures)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for full operational primary banking. A French-regulated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) authorised by the ACPR (e.g., a licensed fintech with an établissement de monnaie électronique status) can legally hold client funds and execute SEPA and SWIFT transfers, but it generally cannot provide credit, trade finance, or foreign exchange advances without a separate credit institution licence. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK or Lithuania-authorised EMIs) may operate temporarily in France under the EU passport if properly registered and supervised, but they are often rejected by procurement clients and tax authorities for large refundable deposits or escrow arrangements. For an industrial boiler refractory contracting SARL, an EMI is viable only for low-value progress collections and FX card payments; core clearing and escrow must sit with a tier-1 credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law (Art. L561-5, Code monétaire et financier) does not mandate a physical in-branch interview when a bank can complete rigorous remote identification via a regulated electronic identification process (Reconnaissance de l'identité à distance) with liveness verification. In practice, major French banks require at least one physical presentation of the legal representative or a video conference interview for SARL clients with non-resident shareholders, in addition to certified true copies of passports, an original Kbis extract, and apostilled corporate resolutions. Remote onboarding is feasible for a wholly French-owned SARL with a French manager; however, when the beneficial owner resides in a third country, a physical or notarised interview at a French consulate is often imposed. The mandatory KYC documentation includes bank-specific forms, a specimen signature card, and a tenancy/business proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder holding >25% of share capital in an opaque offshore jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart and shareholders' register; audited financial statements; evidence of physical corporate substance in jurisdiction; passport and tax residence certificate of the beneficial owner; sworn declaration on source of wealth and source of funds; bank references from the home jurisdiction; notarised and apostilled corporate resolutions approving the French SARL account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent large cash advances or abortive intragroup transfers during the first 12 months of the account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts with milestone descriptions; purchase orders and boiler/refractory materials invoices; proof of customs clearance and VAT treatment; monthly bank narrative and treasury forecast; notice of future transactions exceeding €10,000; sworn statement that no cash payments above €1,000 are made (strict French legal cap).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dealings with counterparties in countries listed as non-cooperative or on targeted EU sanctions list
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trade compliance screening logs; ICC or country-chamber export/import certificates; licenses and end-user declarations for refractory furnace materials destined to industrial thermal facilities; contracts stating no military or dual-use application, aligned with EU dual-use regulation (EU) 2021/821; independent sanctions counsel opinion where necessary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residence mismatches between SARL registered office and beneficial owner's residence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kbis extract; substantiation of a real French establishment (lease, local staff, dedicated material yards, invoicing history); French tax registration certificate; proof of board meeting minutes on French territory; treaty residence certificate for the foreign shareholder (Formulaire 5000 or equivalent); audited accounts substantiating tax filings with French tax authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual high turnover with low employee headcount typical of shell businesses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed payroll registers and French URSSAF filings; subcontracting agreements; health and safety qualification certificates for masonry/refractory works; client certificates from industrial sites; equipment and asset list with serial numbers; operational insurance policies covering worksites.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders or intra-group treasury must be routed via a bank-compliant SWIFT wire with a precise purpose code. For France, the wire must designate either 'Business or commercial purpose (capital contribution)' or a specific BOP code such as 'FXS' or 'Capital Share of Investment' depending on the subscribing bank. A formal 'déclaration de mouvement' for balance of payment statistics is required for each debit/credit in an account with a non-resident when the amount exceeds €50,000, filed via the Banque de France 'BOP' online reporting interface. The supporting verification bundle includes: the signed capital contribution resolution of the SARL; notarised act or written approval if the contribution is in cash; to the extent the injection is quoted on the commercial register, the updated Kbis and M0 business form; bank transfer motive form (OMR) demonstrating the funds are for capital increase or shareholder current account. If the contribution exceeds the authorised capital threshold, certification by a statutory auditor or accountancy body may be required by the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for refractory masonry subcontracts and purchases of heat-resistant ceramic materials settle via SWIFT MT103 priority payment or standard MT103 T/T wire instructions, with mandatory beneficiary details, full VAT treatment, and purpose codes consistent with the French balance-of-payments classification. For high-value procurement, a Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit (revocable or irrevocable at sight, confirmable by a French bank) issued under UCP600 is used, with the French bank acting as issuing or confirming bank. The bank will require a proforma invoice, the original underlying contract, previous import customs documentation for EU-origin purchases, and evidence of compliance with dual-use (materials used for industrial boilers only) end-user declarations. Settlement for domestic EU purchases may be via SEPA Credit Transfer, but for non-EU suppliers SWIFT MT103 with full field 70 remittance information is mandatory. The SARL must ensure that all outbound trade payments reflect the actual 'progress payment' clauses and do not constitute hidden financing with a non-licensed credit institution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Outright Forward Contracts with a French EU-licensed credit institution or OECD-regulated bank
EUR/GBP Outright Forward Contracts for non-EU branch or subcontracting exposure
Delivery-providing foreign exchange swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) used for temporary liquidity conversion over a fixed maturity

Plain vanilla European or American foreign exchange options purchased for hedging, but short option positions strictly prohibited for non-bank treasury price risk unless separately licensed and documented
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD interest and principal exchange) for long-term assets or project-specific bondable contracts denominated in USD

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies (e.g., XOFF markets) only when backed by a real underlying commercial exposure not eligible for physical settlement, lawful under French Oatm/MIFID II rules and the EMIR clearing obligation exemption for commercial hedging
FX collar and combined forward/option structures if the board has approved an annual treasury policy and the transaction passes the 'treasury reasonableness' test under the SARL's business plan

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (filing of approved annual financial statements, management report, and auditor's report if any, with the Commercial Court Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI), updating the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by the associates within six months of the balance sheet date; the approved document set must be filed within one month of approval. For a 31 December closing year, approval must occur by 30 June and filing by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the legal representative to a fine of up to EUR 1,500; a court injunction may impose an astreinte of up to EUR 1,500 per day of delay. Persistent non-filing can trigger administrative strike-off (radiation du registre) and loss of the benefit of legal existence vis-à-vis third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration annuelle de résultat (annual corporate income tax return Form No. 2065 plus the 'liasse fiscale' supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) / Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), filed electronically through the professional e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a SARL with a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year, usually 3 May; SARLs with a non-calendar fiscal year are subject to the corresponding DGFIP filing calendar after the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 5% late-payment penalty on the tax due plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%. If the return remains unfiled 30 days after formal notice, the tax is assessed by summary procedure and the penalty is increased to 10% of the assessed amount.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the balance sheet date: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees exceeding 50. Appointment is also obligatory when the company controls or is controlled by another undertaking unless exempt, or when partners holding at least 1/10 of the capital petition a court to appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory accounts are prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général – PCG) as required by Articles L123-12 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; IFRS may be used only for consolidated statements of listed groups and is not available for standalone SARL statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a stand-alone annual UBO filing. The SARL must maintain an up-to-date beneficial owner register and review its accuracy during the annual accounts approval cycle; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within 30 days of the change. The UBO declaration is not repeated if there is no change, but the beneficial ownership data is confirmed as accurate through the annual accounts deposit process.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des associés), Register of Managers (Registre des gérants), Minute Book (Registre des décisions d'associés)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first €42,000 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover ≤ €10 million and eligible profits; Research Tax Credit (CIR) equal to 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; specific reduced rates for patents and certain renewable assets; loss carryforward with annual cap.
